intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-89 (DEE89) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the GAD1 gene (605363) on chromosome 2q31.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-89 (DEE89) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the GAD1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous variants were identified in five families (Families A, B, D, E and F), whereas compound heterozygous variants were found in Family C (Table 2).
checks.explanation: The paper reports bi-allelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) GAD1 variants as a cause of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. The DEE89 designation is OMIM's own label.

checks.claim: The GAD1 gene is located on chromosome 2q31.
checks.evidence_quote: GAD67 (MIM#605363) is ubiquitously expressed
checks.explanation: The paper does not state the chromosomal location, but your instructions count a gene's chromosomal location as standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-89 (DEE89) is an autosomal recessive neurologic disorder. Seizures begin in the neonatal period or early infancy and are often hard to treat. Affected children have severe global developmental delay and hypotonia. Some patients also have features outside the nervous system, including cleft palate and skeletal abnormalities such as joint contractures, and some have omphalocele.

checks.claim: DEE89 is an autosomal recessive neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: In all families, Sanger sequencing confirmed segregation of the GAD1 variants with the disease phenotype (Supplementary Fig. 1) and a recessive mode of inheritance associated with the disease.
checks.explanation: The paper states recessive inheritance and that all variants are in GAD1, an autosomal gene. It does not use the DEE89 label.

checks.claim: Seizures in DEE89 begin in the neonatal period or early infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: Seizure onset occurred in the first 2 months of life in all patients. All 10 patients, from whom early disease history was available, presented with seizure onset in the first month of life
checks.explanation: Onset was neonatal or in early infancy.

checks.claim: Seizures in DEE89 are often hard to treat.
checks.evidence_quote: Seizures were pharmacologically controlled in three of six affected individuals, with three reported as drug-resistant.
checks.explanation: Half of the patients had drug-resistant seizures, which is consistent with 'often hard to treat'.

checks.claim: Children with DEE89 have severe global developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: All living patients had severe psychomotor delay.
checks.explanation: Stated directly. Intellectual disability was also profound in every patient assessed.

checks.claim: Children with DEE89 have hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: All affected individuals presented with seizures, strongly impaired neurocognitive development, and reduced muscle tone of variable severity.
checks.explanation: The paper reports hypotonia (reduced muscle tone).

checks.claim: Some patients with DEE89 have cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: Interestingly, in addition to neurological features, seven patients presented a cleft palate, six joint contractures and five pes equinovarus.
checks.explanation: Seven of the 11 patients had cleft palate.

checks.claim: Some patients with DEE89 have skeletal abnormalities such as joint contractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Interestingly, in addition to neurological features, seven patients presented a cleft palate, six joint contractures and five pes equinovarus. Scoliosis was reported in four patients.
checks.explanation: Joint contractures, pes equinovarus and scoliosis are all reported.

checks.claim: Some patients with DEE89 have omphalocele.
checks.evidence_quote: Both patients from Family B presented omphalocele
checks.explanation: Two patients had omphalocele.

paragraphs.text: Chatron et al. (2020) reported several patients from multiple unrelated families with biallelic GAD1 variants. They had early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, with seizures starting in the neonatal period or the first months of life, and severe developmental impairment. Many patients also had cleft palate and skeletal or joint abnormalities, including contractures, and some had omphalocele. The authors described the disorder as a neonatal-onset syndromic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

checks.claim: Chatron et al. (2020) reported several patients from multiple unrelated families with biallelic GAD1 variants.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report 11 affected individuals from six unrelated families
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic GAD1 variants reported by Chatron et al. (2020) had early-onset epileptic encephalopathy with seizures starting in the neonatal period or the first months of life.
checks.evidence_quote: Seizure onset occurred in the first 2 months of life in all patients.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic GAD1 variants reported by Chatron et al. (2020) had severe developmental impairment.
checks.evidence_quote: All living patients had severe psychomotor delay.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Many of the patients with biallelic GAD1 variants reported by Chatron et al. (2020) had cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: Seven patients presented a cleft palate and two also had an omphalocele
checks.explanation: Seven of the 11 patients had cleft palate.

checks.claim: Many of the patients with biallelic GAD1 variants reported by Chatron et al. (2020) had skeletal or joint abnormalities, including contractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Eight patients had joint contractures and/or pes equinovarus.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Some of the patients with biallelic GAD1 variants reported by Chatron et al. (2020) had omphalocele.
checks.evidence_quote: Seven patients presented a cleft palate and two also had an omphalocele
checks.explanation: Two patients had omphalocele.

checks.claim: Chatron et al. (2020) described the GAD1-related disorder as a neonatal-onset syndromic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic GAD1 variants cause a neonatal onset syndromic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.explanation: This is the paper's title.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of DEE89 in the families reported by Chatron et al. (2020) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of DEE89 in the families reported by Chatron et al. (2020) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In all families, Sanger sequencing confirmed segregation of the GAD1 variants with the disease phenotype (Supplementary Fig. 1) and a recessive mode of inheritance associated with the disease.
checks.explanation: Stated directly; all families were consanguineous with homozygous variants.

paragraphs.text: In patients with DEE89, Chatron et al. (2020) identified homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the GAD1 gene using exome sequencing. GAD1 encodes GAD67, the main enzyme that makes the neurotransmitter GABA from glutamate. The variants segregated with the disorder in the families. The authors proposed that the disorder results from loss of GAD1 function and reduced GABA synthesis.

checks.claim: Chatron et al. (2020) identified homozygous or compound heterozygous GAD1 variants in patients with DEE89.
checks.evidence_quote: rare homozygous bi-allelic variants in GAD1 were retained as the only likely pathogenic variant in all affected individuals
checks.explanation: Only homozygous variants were identified; no compound heterozygous variants were reported.

checks.claim: Chatron et al. (2020) identified the GAD1 variants in patients with DEE89 by exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: WES was performed for Families A, B, E and F and WGS for Families C and D.
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing was used for four families, but whole-genome sequencing was used for the other two.

checks.claim: GAD1 encodes GAD67, the main enzyme that synthesizes the neurotransmitter GABA from glutamate.
checks.evidence_quote: GAD1 encodes the glutamate decarboxylase enzyme GAD67, a critical actor of the γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) metabolism as it catalyses the decarboxylation of glutamic acid to form GABA.
checks.explanation: The paper describes two GAD isoforms (GAD67 and GAD65) and calls GAD67 the major isoform only at embryonic stages, not 'the main enzyme' overall.

checks.claim: The GAD1 variants identified by Chatron et al. (2020) segregated with DEE89 in the families.
checks.evidence_quote: In all families, Sanger sequencing confirmed segregation of the GAD1 variants with the disease phenotype
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Chatron et al. (2020) proposed that DEE89 results from loss of GAD1 function and reduced GABA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: Vigabatrin inhibits the GABA transaminase, responsible for GABA catabolism, thus increasing the synaptic concentration of GABA reduced by GAD1 variants.
checks.explanation: The paper attributes the disease to bi-allelic loss-of-function variants and describes a constitutive GABA deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Asada et al. (1997) and Condie et al. (1997) found that mice lacking Gad67 had cleft palate and died soon after birth. This is consistent with the cleft palate seen in some patients with DEE89.

checks.claim: Asada et al. (1997) found that mice lacking Gad67 had cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we report the production of GAD67 -/- mice. These mice were born at the expected frequency but died of severe cleft palate during the first morning after birth.
checks.explanation: GAD67-null mice had severe cleft palate.

checks.claim: Asada et al. (1997) found that mice lacking Gad67 died soon after birth.
checks.evidence_quote: These mice were born at the expected frequency but died of severe cleft palate during the first morning after birth.
checks.explanation: The mice died during the first morning after birth.

checks.claim: Cleft palate in Gad67-deficient mice is consistent with the cleft palate seen in some patients with DEE89.
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't discuss human patients or DEE89. The link to cleft palate in patients is the draft's own inference.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Neonatal or early infantile onset seizures
